text:
Tom (customer-sre): Hey, we started getting sporadic 502s and long hangs when our on-prem app calls Redwood Private (VPC). Works fine from home. Happens only when traffic goes via our corp egress proxy.
Lina (Support): Thanks — can you share a minimal repro and whether you see TLS handshake failures vs application-level 502s? Any client logs?
Tom (customer-sre): Minimal repro: curl from inside corp: 
```
curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.private/v1/health
```
Output shows TLS handshake timeout then: "HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway". If we run same curl from laptop off VPN it returns 200.
Ryan (SRE): Sounds like the proxy is terminating TLS or messing with CONNECT. Can you paste the verbose curl output (redacting creds)? Also tcpdump of the initial client hello would help to check SNI.
Tom (customer-sre): Verbose curl snippet: 
```
* Connected to proxy.corp (10.1.2.3) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT api.redwood.private:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.private:443
> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* Proxy replied OK to CONNECT
* Establish HTTP proxy tunnel to api.redwood.private:443
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* server certificate: CN=proxy.corp
* Server certificate does not match 'api.redwood.private'
* closing connection 0
* ERROR: SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.corp' does not match target host name 'api.redwood.private'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.corp' does not match target host name 'api.redwood.private'
```
Tom (customer-sre): tcpdump of initial bytes (client -> proxy) shows client ClientHello without SNI set (empty extension) sometimes; other times it has correct SNI. Very intermittent.
Lina (Support): Interesting — two separate problems could produce that: 1) proxy is doing TLS interception (MITM) and presenting its own cert (CN=proxy.corp) OR 2) proxy is converting the CONNECT into a different flow (terminating/connect-rewrite) and then initiating a downstream TLS session with the proxy's cert. The client sees the proxy cert and fails hostname verification.
Ashley (Eng): If the proxy is actively inspecting, it must preserve SNI on the downstream connection or perform a proper re-issue certificate that matches the downstream hostname (and root trusted by clients). Many corporate TLS inspects don't reissue per-hostnames for private domains. Does the proxy have a trusted root in your client chain?
CorpNet Admin: We do have SSL inspection enabled and issue a corporate CA that clients trust. But we normally preserve SNI; we do have an old rule that rewrites CONNECT to a GET-based tunnel for legacy devices.
Ryan (SRE): The GET-based tunnel is a red flag — some proxies break HTTP CONNECT and upgrade to a back-to-back TLS which can strip or clear the SNI. Can you check if the proxy is switching to non-binary handling? Look for logs showing "CONNECT -> GET tunnel" or header injection like "X-Intercepted: true".
Tom (customer-sre): We found proxy logs showing: 
```
[proxy] conn_id=4523 method=CONNECT target=api.redwood.private:443 -> rewrite=GET path=/tunnel/4523
[proxy] tls_inspect=on rewriter=legacy_tunnel
```
Tom (customer-sre): Also saw headers injected into the upstream request: "Proxy-Client-IP", "X-Forwarded-For", and a custom header "X-SSL-Intercepted: 1".
Lina (Support): OK — that explains it. Two recommendations to unblock quickly: 1) Add an egress bypass rule for api.redwood.private (or the specific IPs) so the proxy performs true CONNECT passthrough / TCP passthrough for 443. 2) If bypass isn't possible, configure the proxy to preserve SNI and avoid rewriting CONNECT into GET/HTTP-layer tunneling for that host.
Ashley (Eng): On Redwood side, we can also add a temporary fallback that accepts connections where client hello SNI is empty and uses the default cert, but that risks exposing multi-tenant cert behavior — not ideal. Better to fix proxy.
CorpNet Admin: We can add a bypass for the customer's private zone. Before we do, what's the smallest IP range we should allow?
Ryan (SRE): Give the Public IP(s) of the Private endpoint backing api.redwood.private. We'll provide them over support DM (don't post here). Also ask them to whitelist TLS port 443 as passthrough (no intercept).
Tom (customer-sre): Trying bypass now. I'll report back.
(10m later) Tom (customer-sre): Bypass applied — calls now consistently return 200. No more CN=proxy.corp in cert. Latency normal.
Lina (Support): Great — marking current issue resolved. We should document this: corporate proxies that rewrite CONNECT to HTTP tunnels or perform TLS inspect without per-host cert reissue often break Private VPC endpoints (SNI/hostname mismatch).
Ashley (Eng): Filing internal note: recommend adding a KB article for customers about proxy TLS inspection, with quick repro commands and required proxy behaviors (CONNECT passthrough or matching re-issued certs + preserved SNI).
CorpNet Admin: FYI we deprecated the legacy tunnel rewriter — we'll push a rule update to avoid rewrites for known vendor endpoints.
Tom (customer-sre): Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Lina (Support): Closing thread — please reopen if it recurs. :white_check_mark:
